sentences.display: Your head is OLDER than your feet.
Most people think time ticks the same for everyone, everywhere.
You sleep on the top bunk, and you age faster than the person below.
You live on a mountain, and your clock runs ahead of the beach.
You stand up, and your head pulls ahead of your toes.
But look at what's actually happening.
Gravity doesn't just pull on you.
The closer you are to Earth, the slower your clock ticks.
In 2010, scientists measured it with two clocks just 33 centimetres apart.
Over a whole lifetime, your head gains about half a *microsecond*.
But GPS satellites feel it every single day.
Without correcting for it, your phone's map would drift by kilometres a day.
So time isn't one clock everyone shares.
Every part of you runs on its own time.
And right now, the top of you is pulling AHEAD.
